title: HCN2 reduces even minor background brain defects in untreated embryos

fields.label: Label
fields.value: HCN2 reduces even minor background brain defects in untreated embryos

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In untreated Xenopus embryos, Hcn2 mRNA injection reduced the incidence of minor deviations from ideal brain morphology from about 9% to about 1.5%, so HCN2 improved patterning beyond that of unperturbed controls.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 overexpression reduces background brain defects

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, misexpression of HCN2 channels resulted in an improvement of developmental patterning even beyond that observed in control populations of unperturbed embryos raised under optimal conditions.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Results › HCN2 overexpression reduces background brain defects”. Scope: Wild-type Xenopus laevis embryos injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA, scored at stage 45

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-10: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proportion contrast is straightforward to test, but the unusually strict morphology endpoint depends on underlying blinded classifications rather than figure summaries. Without deposited individual observations or an independent replication, a decisive reanalysis would require new data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Using blinded embryo-level morphology scores, compare minor-defect proportions between untreated and Hcn2-injected embryos and test the stated reduction from roughly 9% to 1.5% with uncertainty and batch controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No open individual-level morphology dataset is identified.

Minor deviation scoring is subjective and requires blinded raw observations.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.98
discriminating power: 0.82
data existence: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.25

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Incidence, sample size, and a two-group contrast are fully specified. The only public record is the summary in the paper, and using that summary to confirm itself is circular. No phenotype repository contains these unperturbed-versus-HCN2 counts. A new scored cohort, or release of the original calls, is what would resolve the percentages.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: At stage 45, count minor departures from ideal brain morphology in uninjected controls versus uniform Hcn2-WT mRNA injection, with the paper's strict criteria. A drop from about 9% to about 1.5% would confirm the improvement; equal or higher incidence in the injected group would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Clutch and injection effects can change a small baseline rate.

Embryo-level morphology calls are not deposited.

The strict ideal-brain criterion is laboratory-specific and easy to shift.
